sections.markdown:
## A — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
The cover identifies this Wyoming driver manual as the 2021 edition [A01].
The Wyoming Department of Transportation Driver Services Program issues the state's driver licenses [A02].
This dossier covers alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops for the noncommercial passenger-car applicant path.
The handbook says its written test draws on the manual and covers sign recognition, signals, markings, driving laws, safety, crash prevention and vehicle equipment [A03].
No unambiguous written-test question count, passing threshold, bank size or time limit has been verified; these official exam fields remain unknown (verify WY-SEC06-EXAM, WY-SEC06-PASS).
The current issuer page links this edition but warns that print-date information may be outdated; effective date and present applicability need confirmation (verify WY-SEC06-FRESH).
Practice mastery is product policy from the pinned learning loop; it does not establish an official test threshold.

sections.heading: B — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
sections.markdown:
## B — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
Audience: first-time applicants preparing for a Wyoming noncommercial passenger-car written knowledge test, with alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops as this section's subject.
Learning level: beginner. The source scope is the mapped physical pages; explanations use original wording and retain every actor and exception.
The mapped section teaches the staged handbook's impairment and traffic-stop material; it supplies no personalized alcohol-clearance or medication-safety calculation.
This dossier teaches the handbook source; it does not confer a license, replace required exams or establish current eligibility independently.

sections.heading: C — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
sections.markdown:
## C — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
The Driver License Compact is described as a framework for cooperation among states on licensing issues. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
The compact discussion uses the concept of one driver license and one driving record. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
Alcohol slows activity in the brain and spinal cord. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
Alcohol absorbed from the stomach enters the blood and reaches the body, including the brain. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
Larger amounts of alcohol produce a rising blood-alcohol level and more intense impairment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
Blood Alcohol Concentration, or BAC, names the concentration of alcohol in the blood. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
The quantity of alcohol consumed is a factor influencing BAC. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A01
The length of time over which drinking occurs is a factor influencing BAC. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A01
A person's body weight is a factor influencing BAC. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A01
The handbook describes pure ethyl alcohol as a clear, colorless liquid with a burning taste. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A01
Ethyl alcohol mixes readily with other liquids, and adding water or mixer reduces its strength. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A01
The handbook describes beer as usually about five percent alcohol. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A01
The handbook lists wine examples at 12 or 20 percent alcohol. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A01
The handbook describes hard-liquor examples at about 40 to 50 percent alcohol. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A01
The handbook's comparison assigns about one-half ounce of alcohol to a 12-ounce beer, a wine serving of three to five ounces, or an 86-proof liquor serving of one and one-half ounces. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A02
A person may notice alcohol effects soon after drinking starts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A02
Alcohol effects can grow as more alcohol is absorbed into the bloodstream. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A02
Food or milk in the stomach slows alcohol absorption. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A02
Coffee, a shower or exercise does not provide a way to eliminate alcohol faster and sober up sooner. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A02
For the same alcohol amount, a heavier person will likely have a lower BAC than a lighter person because of greater blood and body-fluid volume. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A02
At a BAC of 0.08 percent, a person is impaired mentally and physically even when no outward signs are visible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

sections.domain: Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops — C.02
sections.heading: C — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
sections.markdown:
## C — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A02
Some regular drinkers can conceal outward signs even at relatively high BAC levels. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A03
Increasing BAC further impairs traffic judgment and decision accuracy whether or not the person looks impaired. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A03
Alcohol reduces the ability to identify, predict, decide and execute during driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A03
Alcohol-impaired vision, hearing and body-position sensing reduce a driver's ability to detect traffic hazards. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A03
An impaired driver may fix vision on one object and miss others. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A03
The handbook warns that alcohol impairment can nearly eliminate detection of people and vehicles to the side. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A03
Alcohol reduces hearing and the ability to judge distance. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A03
A high-BAC driver may lose body-position awareness and drift across the centerline, between lanes or off the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A03
Impaired vision, hearing and body-position sensing make predicting other drivers' actions difficult. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A03
Faulty senses, judgments and predictions undermine decisions in critical driving situations. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A03
Alcohol can produce false confidence and poor judgment that contribute to bad driving decisions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A04
The simulator examples describe drink-impaired subjects choosing the wrong turn direction or accelerator instead of brake despite appearing sober. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A04
Even when a drink-impaired driver chooses the correct maneuver, execution may be slower. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A04
The handbook's braking example has a drinking driver at 55 mph travel at least 32 extra feet before applying the brakes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A04
That execution-delay example describes an added two-fifths of a second that can matter even at lower speeds. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A04
Alcohol affects inexperienced drivers more strongly than experienced drivers, and small amounts can sharply increase their errors. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F38 | anchor: A04
Beginning drinkers often show greater impairment after drinking than people with more drinking experience. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F39 | anchor: A04
Unusual weather, lighting or roads increase driving demands while alcohol reduces the ability to meet them. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F40 | anchor: A04
Tiredness, anger, anxiety, emotional upset or elation may already impair a driver before alcohol reduces the ability to compensate. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F41 | anchor: A04
The handbook identifies anger combined with alcohol as particularly dangerous. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0036]

Misconceptions: Looking sober does not establish unimpaired driving, and coffee or a shower does not provide a shortcut to sobriety.
Mnemonics: Recall index: identify, predict, decide, execute; these are the handbook's named driving tasks.
Glossary: Recall terms: blood alcohol concentration, implied consent, controlled drug, probable cause and traffic-stop cooperation.
Dynamic facts: Current compact membership, crash statistics, drug legality and present legal applicability are withheld or retained as freshness debt; no timer is presented as permission to drive.

sections.domain: Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops — C2.01
sections.heading: C2 — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
Driving on a public street or highway is treated under the handbook's Implied Consent discussion as consent to chemical tests for BAC following an impaired-driving arrest. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
If a driver refuses the required chemical test, law enforcement may obtain a warrant for an approved tester to administer it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A01
Submitting to a required test showing BAC at least 0.08 percent leads to a 90-day license and driving-privilege suspension and may also bring criminal penalties. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A01
A DWUI conviction can occur with BAC of 0.05 percent when other supporting evidence is present. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A01
The handbook recommends planning ahead to avoid driving after drinking. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A01
Common diet, sleeping, allergy and tranquilizer drugs can affect skills needed to identify, predict, decide or execute while driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A01
Diet and stay-awake pills may create false alertness and confidence that encourage excessive risk-taking. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A01
Stay-awake drugs can hide fatigue without restoring the ability to identify hazards and make quick decisions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A01
Sleeping pills can cause sleepiness and make thinking and emotional control difficult. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A01
Sleeping pills can affect the driving decision tasks for several hours. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A02
Allergy and cold remedies can contain antihistamines, bromides, codeine or alcohol and may cause sleepiness or impaired thinking. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A02
Tranquilizers can reduce alertness, cause sleepiness and impair thinking, emotions, attention, judgment and reactions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A02
The handbook says tranquilizer effects may continue for several hours. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A02
The mind-altering drugs discussed can vary in purity and strength, making their overall effects unpredictable. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A02
The mind-altering drugs discussed can affect mood, vision, reaction and judgments of time or space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A02
A person under the influence of the discussed mind-altering drugs must not attempt to drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A02
Do not drive after starting a new medicine until you are certain it will not impair driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A02
The handbook warns that driving under the influence of a controlled drug can lead to a DWUI charge and conviction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A02
Ask the prescribing doctor how a prescribed drug might affect driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R20 | anchor: A02
Read the label carefully before buying or using a nonprescription drug. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R21 | anchor: A02
A traffic stop may be intended to warn about danger, address a traffic violation or investigate a vehicle matching a crime-related description. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-R22 | anchor: A03
An officer may also stop a driver who appears to need help or may have witnessed a crime. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

sections.domain: Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops — C2.02
sections.heading: C2 — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Alcohol, drugs and law enforcement stops
FACT_ID: sec06-R23 | anchor: A03
When police lights or a siren indicate a stop, stay calm, slow down and pull to a safe place on the road's right side. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R24 | anchor: A03
During the stop, avoid halting in a travel lane, on a bridge or against a guardrail. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R25 | anchor: A03
After stopping, put the vehicle in park. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R26 | anchor: A03
For communication during the stop, lower the window, finish phone calls and reduce the radio volume. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R27 | anchor: A03
Remain in the vehicle unless the officer directs otherwise, and wait for instructions about staying in or exiting. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R28 | anchor: A03
Keep your hands visible to the officer on the steering wheel. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R29 | anchor: A03
The handbook says an officer will generally provide a name on request and explain the reason for the stop, while recognizing that circumstances differ. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R30 | anchor: A03
Tell the officer about weapons and their locations without reaching or pointing toward them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R31 | anchor: A03
Avoid sudden movements, especially toward the floor, rear seat or passenger side. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R32 | anchor: A03
Turn on the vehicle's interior light for a nighttime stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R33 | anchor: A03
Carry the driver license, proof of insurance and vehicle registration and show them when the officer requests them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec06-R34 | anchor: A04
If documents are out of reach, tell the officer where they are before reaching for them. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R35 | anchor: A04
Encourage passengers to stay quiet and cooperate with instructions during the stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R36 | anchor: A04
The handbook places responsibility for the vehicle and its occupants on the operator. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R37 | anchor: A04
Answer the officer's questions truthfully. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R38 | anchor: A04
If a ticket's reason is unclear, politely ask the officer to explain it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R39 | anchor: A04
Avoid arguing about the violation during the stop; a contested matter can be addressed in court. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R40 | anchor: A04
The handbook says a driver may politely refuse consent to a vehicle search, but an officer may search without that consent when probable cause exists. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R41 | anchor: A04
For a roadside emergency or maintenance vehicle with activated lights on an interstate, the handbook directs drivers to merge into the lane farthest from it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R42 | anchor: A04
On a two-lane road, the handbook's roadside emergency-or-maintenance-vehicle instruction calls for reducing speed by at least 20 mph when its lights are activated. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R43 | anchor: A04
When an emergency vehicle with activated lights overtakes you, move to the right side and stop until it has passed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0040]
